Rachel / Marissa — draft legal position below. High-level approach: keep 'right to defend' with Redwood for third-party claims that relate to our model outputs, but carve customer-supplied content into a narrower bucket where customer must either: (a) defend and indemnify, or (b) trigger an escrow / insurance-first waterfall for claims attributable to their data/prompts.

Proposal (for order form language):
- Allocation: Redwood will defend third-party IP claims alleging infringement by the hosted model output, unless the claim reasonably arises from: (i) customer-provided training data or prompts; or (ii) customer instructions that require the model to reproduce third-party copyrighted material. For (i) and (ii), customer must either assume defense or: (A) activate an escrow equal to 3x average monthly spend (min $50k) within 10 business days of notice, or (B) have an active policy that satisfies the following: primary commercial general liability (CGL) + technology E&O with a minimum per-claim limit of $2M naming Redwood as additional insured.

- Defense control: Redwood retains the right to participate in the defense and to approve settlements that impose obligations on Redwood. If customer elects to control the defense, Redwood may require reasonable bond or escrow to secure customer obligations.

- Evidence checklist (attach to order form):
  * Signed notice with claim details and alleged infringed works
  * Customer original prompt/data sample and timestamped usage record from their tenant
  * Proof of customer ownership or license for the disputed content (where available)
  * Any correspondence from claimant

- Escrow release: escrow is released pro rata after claim resolution; disputed portion held until final disposition.

Attached: Evidence_Template_v2.xlsx (evidence fields that ops needs).

Commercial note: 3x monthly spend / $50k floor is an opening number — Ben, flag if this kills the deal on pricing/AR. Marissa, LMK if Ops can enforce collection and triage on a 10 business day SLA.

Kimberly Park

Subject: Re: Veridian redlines (MSA + order form) — IP indemnity (proposal)

Tom / Elisabeth — thanks for the redlines and for the patience. Our internal review surfaced a workable path we think meets Veridian's commercial comfort while keeping Redwood's operational and liability guardrails intact. Summary of our counterproposal: 

1) Allocation buckets:
  - Model-output claims: Redwood will defend and (subject to usual limitations) indemnify.
  - Customer-supplied data/prompts: customer to assume liability by default. If customer wants Redwood to take on defense for these claims, they must either provide (i) proof of insurance (see Kimberly's thresholds) or (ii) post escrow.

2) Escrow / insurance waterfall (order form option):
  - Escrow = 3x customer's average monthly Redwood spend (calculated from trailing 3 months), with a $50k minimum.
  - Insurance-first: customer must present active E&O/CGL with $2M per-claim limit naming Redwood as additional insured; Redwood will use insurance proceeds before drawing escrow.
  - Escrow activation: customer has 10 business days from notice to fund escrow; failure to fund permits Redwood to suspend affected services for the specific customer tenant until funded or alternative security is provided.

3) Defense control & settlement: Redwood retains participation and prior written consent rights for settlements that impose obligations on Redwood. If customer controls defense, Redwood may require a bond / escrow to secure Redwood's exposure.

4) Evidence & triage: We will require the Evidence_Template fields to be completed; Ops will open triage within 48 hours of a complete evidence pack.

Next steps if you can live with the framework: 1) confirm whether Veridian wants escrow or insurance-first in the order form (we can offer both as options); 2) if escrow, provide an estimated monthly spend to let us calculate the escrow amount; 3) we will convert to redline and circulate.

If helpful, Kimberly and I are available for a 30-minute call tomorrow to run through examples (sample takedown + evidence flow).

Best,
Rachel Kim
Sr. Manager, Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference
